extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and attorneys subject to USPTO disciplinary proceedings (OED/OED Director; USPTO enforcement staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Final order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24: identifies the basis for discipline (state ethical suspension), the procedural notice/response framework, the factual misconduct underlying the state suspension, and the sanctions and administrative steps the USPTO will take.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a state's disciplinary authority when a practitioner has been suspended on ethical grounds by that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order is mailed to the practitioner notifying them that the Director has filed a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting imposition of identical discipline; the Notice provides an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on reasons in 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1). If the practitioner does not file a response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation predicate: 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h) (suspension by state)
rubrics_metrics.description: Being suspended on ethical grounds from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State constitutes a ground for discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the USPTO action is 'for violating 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h), predicated upon being suspended on ethical grounds from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.' This predicate supports imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement: Notice delivery and 40-day response period
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must mail a Notice and Order (certified mail used in this case) and provide the respondent forty (40) days to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified-mail receipt is recorded; failure to file a response within the 40-day period may be treated as an absence of any genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d), enabling the Director to order the suspension without further factual dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-law professional-conduct violations constituting grounds for suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific attorney misconduct (as found by the state disciplinary authority) that supported the state suspension: violations of state Rules of Professional Conduct (Arizona Rules 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.16, 8.1(b), and 8.4(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists concrete misconduct that led to the state suspension: accepting advanced payment to prosecute a patent application but neglecting to prosecute it; failing to communicate with or respond to client inquiries; allowing the patent application to become abandoned without the client's authorization; vacating his office without notice to the client; failing to return any unearned fees for legal work not performed. These factual findings are used as the predicate for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction imposed: suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may suspend a practitioner from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non‑patent law before the USPTO for a period identical to the state-imposed suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, the Director ordered suspension for six (6) months and one (1) day, effective the date of the Final Order. The order explicitly states the scope (patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters) and effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice requirements (37 C.F.R. §11.59 and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish notice of the discipline in the Official Gazette and give notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where the respondent is admitted, and the public pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires publication of a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette and posting disciplinary decisions for public reading in the OED Reading Room (with URL given). It also requires notice to disciplinary agencies and courts where respondent is admitted and known to be admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑suspension duties (37 C.F.R. §11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent who is suspended must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. §11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs the respondent to comply with the duties in §11.58, although it does not restate those duties in full. (Practitioners must consult §11.58 for the specific obligations imposed during suspension.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative sanctions on USPTO accounts and PKI
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and associated public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates, and prohibit obtaining or being added to a Customer Number until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order: (1) dissociates the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the PKI certificate associated with those Customer Numbers; (2) directs that the respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory authority for action (35 U.S.C. §32; 37 C.F.R. §§11.24, 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary actions and the procedures for reciprocal discipline are taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §32 and implementing regulations 37 C.F.R. §§11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutory/regulatory provisions as the basis for the USPTO's authority to impose reciprocal discipline and to publish/notify regarding disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond: determination of no genuine issue of material fact (37 C.F.R. §11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent fails to file a timely response to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and proceed to impose the reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly states that in light of the respondent's failure to file a response, 'there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and suspension ... is the appropriate discipline.' This establishes the practical consequence of non‑response in reciprocal proceedings.
